speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have significant shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation or a feeling of fullness after eating small amounts of food?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Ascites and Pleural Effusion. Given your history of being nulliparous and the rapid onset of shortness breath and abdominal distension with a known ovarian mass, these findings are highly suggestive of advanced ovarian malignancy causing fluid accumulation in the abdomen and chest. We will proceed with imaging and tumor markers to confirm the stage and guide treatment.
